title: The Beach That Walks Sideways
question: How do waves move sand and reshape a coast?
hook: Every wave that rolls in at a slant nudges the beach a little further down the shore.
idea: Waves are the coast's main shapers: their strength decides whether sand is added or taken, and their angle carries it along the shore.

beats.prompt: Waves keep arriving at a slant to the beach. A grain of sand is picked up by one wave, dropped, and picked up again by the next. After many waves, where is it?

choices.label: Right back where it started
choices.feedback: It is tempting to think in and out cancel, but the water comes in at an angle and goes back straight, so each trip leaves a sideways step.

choices.label: Farther along the beach, in one direction
Far out at sea, past the waves
choices.feedback: The backwash drops its sediment as it loses energy, so the grain stays on the beach rather than being flung offshore.

choices.label: High up the beach, past the tide line
choices.feedback: The swash pushes sand up the slope, but gravity pulls the water and sand back down each time.

beats.explain: Swash carries sand up the beach at an angle, backwash drops it straight back down, and the next wave pushes it on again, so sediment moves steadily in one direction.

beats.prompt: Put the steps of longshore drift in order.
items: A wave hits the shore at an angle and picks up sand
The swash carries the sand up the beach at an angle
The backwash falls straight back and drops the sand
The next wave picks up the sand and pushes it further along
beats.explain: Each wave's slanted swash and straight backwash shift sand a little sideways, and the next wave repeats it.

beats.prompt: Sort each description into the kind of wave it belongs to.
items: Carry sediment out to bars under the sea
Pile sediment up onto the berm
beats.explain: Strength sets the effect: strong winter waves remove sediment from the beach, while weak summer waves build it up.

beats.prompt: Match each coastal feature to how it forms.
pairs: A glacial valley flooded by the sea
A river valley flooded by the sea
Sand blown up the beach by onshore winds
Sediment bound together by calcium carbonate
beats.explain: Rising seas, wind and chemistry all add their own landforms to the ones that waves make.
